newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Courtaulds profit seen slightly up. [CORRECTED 11:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Courtaulds profit seen slightly up. [CORRECTED 11:20 GMT]

text.p: British chemicals group Courtaulds Plc is expected to announce a modest advance in full-year pre-tax profit on Wednesday (corrects from Tuesday), with the rampant pound and sickly viscose market casting a shadow over the results.
Analysts' forecasts for pre-tax profit are in a narrow range of between 132.0 and 136.0 million stg compared with 131.5 million stg in the year to March 1996.
The dividend is expected to rise to between 16.40 pence and 16.50 pence from 16.05 pence per share.

The strength of the pound, which has cut a swathe through the profits of British industry in recent months, will act as a major restraint on Courtaulds. Some 85 percent of the group's sales are outside Britain.

Courtaulds warned in February that the strength of sterling and the sale of four non-core operations last year would blunt the impact of trading improvements at most of its core businesses, which include industrial coatings and sealants and consumer packaging.

The second drag on progress continues to be viscose, where profits and prices have been hit by global overcapacity and declining demand. The company has indicated that there are some signs of recovery in viscose, but nothing to get elated about.

Analysts will be watching for reassurance that the group's plans to introduce new production capacity for its highly successful new fibre Tencel are on course. An announcement of the siting of new Tencel capacity in Asia is expected later this year.
Courtaulds has had a difficult year, with its share price falling from a 12-month high of 490 pence last October to trade close to its lows around 320 pence on Friday morning.

Paul Diggle, director of equity research at SocGen, said: "The message is quite important that they are taking costs out of the business and that Tencel is growing profitably and new capacity is on schedule."
Diggle said that although the current year looks dull, analysts had welcomed the more open approach of Courtauld's new management team, led by chief executive Gordon Campbell.
